forecasting_formulation: Targets are next-day AQI and next-day AQI bucket, per city. Features may use measurements dated today or earlier for that city only.

leakage_controls.temporal: The split is a fixed calendar boundary; shuffle is never used. TimeSeriesSplit is used for cross-validation. Lags and rolling windows are computed with groupby('City') so no city contributes to another city's history, and no window extends past the current day.
leakage_controls.target: AQI_next and AQI_Bucket_next are mutually excluded from each other's feature matrix, and an assertion in build_feature_matrix fails the run if either appears among the candidates. Same-day AQI and AQI_Bucket_ordinal are retained as legitimate predictors because they are known at prediction time; the distinct same-day nowcast leakage is demonstrated empirically in models/train_classification.py.
leakage_controls.encoder: The encoding is fitted on the training period only. Applying a full-sample city mean would allow each test row to contribute to the value of its own encoded feature.
leakage_controls.scaler: Scaling is performed inside a scikit-learn Pipeline so that fit_transform touches training folds only; no scaler is ever fitted on the test partition.
leakage_controls.imputation: All imputation statistics were estimated on pre-boundary rows in src/data/clean.py, and the adopted strategy uses no forward-looking information within a city's series.

event_flags.covid_policy: The 2020 lockdown is modelled with an explicit flag rather than excluded. The flag lets a model represent the regime change instead of averaging over it, and the period is additionally reported as a separate stress-test slice of the test set in results/evaluation_regression.json and results/evaluation_classification.json, so that its contribution to the headline error is visible rather than hidden.

city_target_encoding.leakage_note: The encoding is fitted on the training period only. Applying a full-sample city mean would allow each test row to contribute to the value of its own encoded feature.

ordinal_encoding.justification: The CPCB buckets are ordered severity categories, so an ordinal code preserves the ordering that a one-hot encoding would discard. The ordinal form is used for the ordered-severity features; the classification target itself is kept as the string label so that per-class metrics remain readable.
